media.alt: Coronary angiography is the gold standard test for determining the extent and severity of coronary artery disease

content.text: "Coronary angiography was first performed 40 years ago, and remains the gold standard test for diagnosis of coronary artery disease, against which other diagnostic tests arc validated", revealed Dr Asad Pathan. Consultant Clinical and Interventional Cardiologist of the Aga Khan University Hospital (AKUH). He was giving a presentation on "Coronary Angiography" at "Signs, Symptoms and Care", a monthly public health awareness program, held on May 8. 1999 at AKUH Dr Path an added, "angiography is currently the only established method for accurately assessing the extent and severity of coronary artery disease",

Labelling coronary artery, disease as a major cause of illness and deaths in Pakistan, Dr Pathanexplained that this disease leads to the narrowing of the blood vessels of the heart and is a slowly progressing process that may remain clinically unapparent for long periods of time. Coronary disease often becomes clinically evident because of the occurrence of symtoms such as angina or those associated with a heart attack or even sudden death. Dr Pathan stressed on the early detection of the disease and mentioned that coronary angiography is a reliable and safe procedure with a trivial but definable risk. The information obtained from angiography provides diagnostic information and is invaluable in making appropriate decisions about therapeutic interventions such as angioplasty or bypass surgery, which leads to relief of angina and can improve the long term outcome in some patients.
A panel of Consultant Cardiologists also participated in the panel discussion. This included Dr Khawar Abbass Kazmi, Dr Anwar Ahmed and Dr Momina Mastoor.
